name: PM-KUSUM: Solar Pumps for Farmers
status_note: Phase 1 now continues only for already-sanctioned projects (completion deadline 31 March 2027), and the follow-up PM-KUSUM 2.0 had not been launched as of late October 2026. New farmer applications are accepted only where your state still has sanctioned solar-pump quota. Ask your state nodal agency before spending time on this.
summary: Subsidy for installing a stand-alone solar irrigation pump, or for solarising an existing grid-connected pump, to cut diesel and electricity costs.

benefits.headline: Up to about 60% subsidy on a solar pump (farmer pays about 40%, or only 10% upfront with a bank loan)
details: Central subsidy of 30% of the benchmark/tender cost plus a state subsidy of at least 30%; the farmer pays the remaining 40%, and bank finance can cover part of it.
In North-eastern states, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kashmir/Ladakh and island territories the central subsidy is 50% and the state share at least 30%.
Central subsidy is limited to pumps of up to 7.5 HP. Small and marginal farmers get priority.

summary: You are a farmer (individual, group, cooperative or water-user association) with agricultural land.
You have a water source you can pump from (borewell/tubewell, open well, pond or river).
Stand-alone solar pump: best suited if you irrigate with a diesel pump or have no grid connection. Solarisation of an existing pump: you already have a grid-connected agricultural pump.

You have a grid-connected pump, so ask about solarising it (and selling surplus power to the DISCOM).
Small and marginal farmers are given priority by the state implementing agencies.

steps: Ask your state's implementing agency (usually the state renewable energy development agency, Agriculture department or DISCOM) if applications are open in your district.
Apply on the state's PM-KUSUM portal or at the district office with your documents.
Pay your share (or arrange it with a bank loan) once the application is approved.
An empanelled vendor installs the pump; get an inspection certificate and keep your bills.
offline: State renewable energy agency / DISCOM office

deadline.text: No open national application window. Phase 1 projects must be completed by 31 March 2027, and new rounds depend on your state or the upcoming PM-KUSUM 2.0.

caveats: Subsidy shares differ by state; the percentages above are the national scheme pattern.
